is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.s. (Muleba-Kis strain, outcrossed with An. gambiae Kisumu) (Page 1, Abstract; Page 5, Section 2.4).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper genotypes Vgsc L1014S (kdr-east / L995S) and Ace-1 G119S (G280S) (Page 6, Section 2.6.2; Page 9, Table 1).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 on Page 9 provides percentage frequencies of homozygous mutant (%RRe), heterozygous (%RSe), and homozygous susceptible (%SSe) alongside sample sizes for multiple generations (G43 to G204).

african_field_population.evidence: Genotyping data in the paper are solely reported for laboratory-maintained generations (G43 to G204) of an artificial outcrossed colony (Muleba wild males crossed with Kisumu laboratory females) under lab insecticide selection. No field-caught adults (F0), wild larvae reared to adult, or F1 field progeny were genotyped in this paper (Page 5, Section 2.4; Page 9, Table 1).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study describing the establishment, maintenance, and molecular/phenotypic characterization of the Muleba-Kis colony.

sub_country_location.evidence: Original wild parent mosquitoes were collected in Kyamyorwa (02°04′27.5″ S, 31°34′10.8″ E) and Kiteme (02°03′20.9″ S, 31°27′16.8″ E) in Muleba district, northwest Tanzania (Page 4, Section 2.1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The colony was established in 2012–2013 and maintained/monitored across generations from 2013 through 2020 (Page 4, Section 2.1; Page 5, Section 2.4; Page 10, Table 2), spanning >7 years without specific collection years given for each tested generation in Table 1.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper characterizes a locally established reference colony at the KCMUCo-PAMVERC insectary.

supplement.evidence: All colony genotyping and bioassay results are reported within the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study describes the colonization, outcrossing with the susceptible Kisumu strain, pyrethroid selection, and long-term authentication of the Anopheles gambiae s.s. Muleba-Kis colony over 200 generations. Because all extractable genotype data are derived from advanced generations (G43–G204) of a laboratory colony rather than African field populations (F0/F1), the study does not meet inclusion criteria.
